staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the saved AddressSanitizer crash against this vulnerable CPython checkout in the ARVO workspace.

bug_description.original: An off by 1 error exists in the f string tokenizer, which can lead to incorrect parsing of f-strings.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / poc
bug_description.normalized: The saved witness file is 14,424 bytes, but `fuzz_ast_literal_eval` only requires that some `\0` appear within `size` and then calls `PyUnicode_FromString(data)`, so the parser/tokenizer consumes only the 7,338-byte prefix before the first NUL. That consumed prefix contains 222 single-quoted f-string starts `f'{` and zero `}` bytes; the remaining 7,085 bytes after the first NUL are off-path for this crash. After the malformed prefix first raises generic `invalid syntax`, `_PyPegen_tokenize_full_source_to_check_for_errors()` continues tokenization on the same `tok_state`. Along that path, each consumed `f'` executes `tok_get_normal_mode()`'s `f_string_quote` branch and each following single `{` in `tok_get_fstring_mode()` switches back to regular mode for the inner expression without popping an older f-string mode. Because the consumed prefix has no `}` bytes, the brace-return logic and `tok->tok_mode_stack_index--` pop do not run before the next inner `f'`. Once 199 active f-string modes have accumulated, `tokenizer_mode *the_current_tok = TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok);` at `Parser/tokenizer.c:2204` preincrements `tok->tok_mode_stack_index` to 200 even though the vulnerable `tok_mode_stack` has only `MAXLEVEL = 200` elements (indexes 0 through 199). The next assignment `the_current_tok->f_string_quote = quote;` at line 2206 writes one byte past the heap-allocated `struct tok_state`, and AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE there. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by checking `tok->tok_mode_stack_index + 1 >= MAXFSTRINGLEVEL` before `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` and raising `too many nested f-strings` instead.

source.description: Source. `fuzz_ast_literal_eval` materializes the fuzz buffer as a Python Unicode object; because it uses `PyUnicode_FromString`, every later parser/tokenizer step sees only the bytes before the first NUL.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` file is 14,424 bytes, but `fuzz_ast_literal_eval` only requires `memchr(data, '\0', size) != NULL`. Its first `\0` is at offset 7338, so `PyUnicode_FromString(data)` and all downstream parser/tokenizer logic consume only the 7,338-byte prefix before that NUL. That consumed prefix contains 222 `f'{` substrings and zero `}` bytes; the 7,085 bytes after the first NUL do not reach the tokenizer on the crashing path.

root_cause.description: Missing bounds check. `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` preincrements `tok->tok_mode_stack_index` and returns `&tok->tok_mode_stack[new_index]` without verifying that another f-string mode slot exists.
root_cause.note: In the vulnerable tree `tok_new()` initializes `tok->tok_mode_stack_index = 0` and the destination array is `tokenizer_mode tok_mode_stack[MAXLEVEL];` with `MAXLEVEL = 200`, so valid indexes are 0 through 199. The first-NUL-truncated witness contains 222 `f'{` starts and zero `}` bytes, so before the crashing start it can accumulate 199 active nested f-string modes without a pop. This line's `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` expansion preincrements the index to 200 and yields a one-past-end pointer. The patch inserts `if (tok->tok_mode_stack_index + 1 >= MAXFSTRINGLEVEL) { return MAKE_TOKEN(syntaxerror(tok, "too many nested f-strings")); }` immediately before this line and resizes the stack to `MAXFSTRINGLEVEL`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The one-past-end `the_current_tok` pointer from the unchecked push is dereferenced and a byte is written outside the heap-allocated `tok_state` object.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `WRITE of size 1` at `Parser/tokenizer.c:2206:41` on address `0x628000007e34`, 4 bytes to the right of the 15,664-byte region allocated for `struct tok_state` in `tok_new()` at `Parser/tokenizer.c:74`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Each consumed `f'{` start in the 7,338-byte prefix reaches this branch as a candidate nested f-string start. Because that same consumed prefix contains zero `}` bytes, these attacker-controlled starts can keep requesting deeper tokenizer-mode slots until the 200th push overflows `tok_mode_stack`.

parser_admitted.description: The first-NUL-truncated Unicode string from `PyUnicode_FromString(data)` has already been admitted into CPython's parser/tokenizer pipeline and wrapped in a live `tok_state` before the later error-handling tokenization path reaches the crash.

evidence_limitations: `trace_feedback.json` required only static witness corrections, and `run_flags.json` keeps `runtime_disambiguation` false, so Stage 02 rebuilt the chain from staged source, the saved `poc` bytes, the reproduction report, and the saved AddressSanitizer trace without adding instrumentation.

The exact byte offset of the crashing 200th nested `f'` within the 7,338-byte consumed prefix was not measured dynamically. The source-level chain is still closed because that consumed prefix has 222 `f'{` starts and zero `}` bytes, which is sufficient to exceed the 200-entry vulnerable stack before any pop.
Stage 02 does not build or execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though `patch.diff` adds the exact missing nesting guard before `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)`.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz target accepts the saved witness because some `\0` appears within `size`, then `PyUnicode_FromString(data)` truncates at the first NUL and `ast.literal_eval` compiles only the 7,338-byte prefix before that NUL.
Because that malformed consumed prefix first produces generic `invalid syntax`, pegen enters its tokenizer-error pass and asks `_PyTokenizer_Get()` for more tokens on the same `tok_state`.

Within the 7,338-byte consumed prefix, repeated `f'{` pairs alternate `tok_get_normal_mode()` and `tok_get_fstring_mode()`: each `f'` starts another f-string mode and each following single `{` switches back to regular mode for the inner expression. Because the consumed prefix contains no `}` bytes, earlier modes are not popped before the next inner `f'`.

With 199 active f-string modes already accumulated, `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` increments the stack index to 200 without a guard and the subsequent `the_current_tok->f_string_quote = quote` write overruns the heap-allocated `tok_state`, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE.

fine_trace.note: Source. After `memchr(data, '\0', size) != NULL` admits the witness, `PyUnicode_FromString` uses `strlen` semantics and materializes only the bytes before the first NUL. On the saved `poc` the first NUL is at offset 7338, so the parser sees a 7,338-byte prefix containing 222 `f'{` substrings and no `}`; bytes after that NUL are off-path for this crash.
The first-NUL-truncated Python source from step 1 is copied into tokenizer-owned storage as `translated`; later tokenization reads the same consumed prefix from this buffer.
Tokenizer cursor state is pointed at the copied buffer, making the consumed prefix the active character stream for later `_PyTokenizer_Get()` calls.

After the malformed consumed prefix first raises generic `invalid syntax`, pegen explicitly asks the tokenizer for more tokens to look for tokenizer-specific errors. The saved crash stack reaches the overflow through this second-pass call chain: `_PyPegen_tokenize_full_source_to_check_for_errors -> _PyTokenizer_Get -> tok_get -> tok_get_normal_mode`.

fine_trace.code:
if (((tolower(*tok->start) == 'f' || tolower(*tok->start) == 'r') && (c == '\'' || c == '"'))) {
    int quote = c;
fine_trace.note: Whenever the active regular-mode stream begins with another consumed `f'`, this branch treats it as a new f-string start and captures the quote character for a new mode slot. The 7,338-byte consumed prefix contains 222 such `f'{` starts before the first NUL.

For each just-opened f-string, the following single `{` increments `current_tok->curly_bracket_expr_start_depth`, flips the current mode back to `TOK_REGULAR_MODE`, and immediately recurses into `tok_get_normal_mode()` for the inner expression. Because the consumed prefix has no `}` bytes, the `c == '}'` return-to-fstring path at `Parser/tokenizer.c:2431-2433` and the pop at line 2501 do not execute before the next inner `f'`.

Root cause. Repeating the step-5 and step-6 pattern on the consumed prefix accumulates active f-string modes without a pop until `tok->tok_mode_stack_index == 199`. This line's `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` expansion preincrements the index to 200 and returns `&tok->tok_mode_stack[200]` even though the vulnerable declaration is `tokenizer_mode tok_mode_stack[MAXLEVEL];` with `MAXLEVEL = 200`, so the returned pointer is one element past the array inside the heap-allocated `struct tok_state` from `tok_new()`.

Sink. The one-past-end pointer from step 7 is dereferenced and the quote byte is written into the redzone beyond `struct tok_state`. AddressSanitizer reports this exact statement as `WRITE of size 1` at `Parser/tokenizer.c:2206:41`.

poc.trigger: Use the saved Stage 01 reproduction command from `reproduction_report.json`: `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_58295 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`. The vulnerable `fuzz_ast_literal_eval` target accepts the saved witness because `memchr(data, '\0', size)` finds a NUL, then `PyUnicode_FromString(data)` turns only the 7,338-byte prefix before that first NUL into Python source for `ast.literal_eval`. That exact consumed prefix reproduces the AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow in `tok_get_normal_mode`.

format.name: Python source bytes truncated at first NUL
format.contract: This exact witness needs only to contain a NUL within the supplied `size`; on the saved file the first `\0` is at offset 7338, so `PyUnicode_FromString(data)` makes the parser consume only bytes `[0, 7338)`. That consumed prefix contains 222 `f'{` starts and zero `}` bytes, which is sufficient for the tokenizer-error pass to attempt a 200th `TOK_NEXT_MODE(tok)` push before any pop. Bytes after the first NUL are not consumed on this crashing path.
